title: 9 Features to Look for in Attendance Tracking Software
summary: Choosing attendance tracking software? Learn the 9 features that cut payroll errors, deter time theft, and reduce compliance risk for your business.
body_markdown:
Listen to the article: 9 Features to Look for in Attendance Tracking Software


8:38


Attendance tracking sounds like a back-office chore. It isn’t, and it’s actually directly connected to your business's risk profile. In fiscal year 2025, the Department of Labor “[recovered more than $259 million in back wages for nearly 177,000 employees nationwide – an average of $1,465 per worker](https://www.dol.gov/newsroom/releases/whd/whd20260108) .” And many wage-and-hour problems start with the same culprit: inaccurate time records.


Accurate attendance tracking is an important part of your defense strategy. Here’s what we’ll cover:


- Why attendance tracking matters
- 9 features to look for in attendance tracking software
- How PEO time and attendance options compare
- How a PEO strengthens attendance tracking


Let’s start with the why.


## Why Does Attendance Tracking Matter for Small Businesses?


The Fair Labor Standards Act requires employers to record “hours worked each day” and “total hours worked each workweek” for every non-exempt employee. In the[Department of Labor’s words](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/fact-sheets/21-flsa-recordkeeping) , “the law requires[this information](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/fix-payroll-problems-source-time-tracking-software) to be accurate.” Those records generally need to stick around for at least three years. So a scribbled timesheet or a “close enough” estimate is a liability with a paper trail.


## What Features Should Attendance Tracking Software Have?


There’s no one-size-fits-all attendance tracking setup. A five-person landscaping crew, a 60-person restaurant, and a franchise with[multiple locations](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/multi-location-payroll-what-franchise-owners-need-know) all need different features. But the following five capabilities belong on every buyer’s checklist.


1. **Scheduling that connects to your time data.** If your employees work in shifts, scheduling is your first line of defense against surprise overtime. It doesn’t have to live inside your attendance tracking tool, but it should connect to it so planned hours and actual hours tell the same story. Heads up: Oregon and approximately 10 cities, including Chicago and New York City, require covered employers to post schedules in advance.
2. **Clock-in options that fit your workforce.** Not everyone works at a desk. Look for web and mobile clock-ins at minimum, plus biometric options if your team shares a worksite. Offline options become important when employees encounter cell reception issues, reducing the need for manual corrections later.
3. **Time-theft prevention.** Buddy punching, or clocking in for a coworker, is more common than you’d think. In a[July 2026 survey](https://www.wftv.com/news/time-theft-report/SF4F7UB7PY677GFBEXZISEXSSA/) of 831 hourly workers, “one in 4 (or 25% of) hourly employees in the survey has engaged in buddy punching over the past 12 months.” Geofencing, which limits punches to a set location, and biometric verification make buddy-punching much harder to pull off. One catch: collecting fingerprints or face scans can trigger state consent laws, like Illinois’ Biometric Information Privacy Act.
4. **Mobile access and self-service.** Employees clock in, view their hours, and handle routine requests from their phones without calling the office. Less chasing, more actual work.
5. **PTO tracking that syncs with payroll.** Time off and hours worked should connect to payroll. When PTO balances live in a separate spreadsheet, today’s tracking slip becomes tomorrow’s payroll mistake, and with paid leave rules varying by state and city, those slips add up fast.


These five features keep your day-to-day running smoothly, but the features that really earn their keep are the ones that protect you when something goes sideways.


## Which Features Protect You From Payroll & Compliance Risk?


These four features turn attendance data into a defense against payroll errors and wage-and-hour claims.


1. **Overtime, break, and compliance alerts.** Real-time alerts flag employees approaching overtime before it happens, not after payroll runs. Look for meal and rest break rules, missed-punch notifications, and shift-end attestations, where employees confirm with a quick “yes” or “no” that they took their breaks. That’s a documented answer you’ll be glad to have if questions come up later.
2. **Payroll integration.** More than just PTO, approved hours and overtime should also flow straight into payroll. Every time someone re-keys numbers from one system into another, there’s a fresh chance for a typo to become a paycheck error.
3. **Reporting and analytics.** Look for overtime reports by department, absenteeism patterns, labor costs versus budget, and job costing. Good reports turn attendance tracking from recordkeeping into planning, so you can spot the crew that always seems to hit overtime or the project that keeps running over budget.
4. **Centralized, secure records that**[grow with you](https://www.bbsi.com/business-owner-resources/peo-vs-in-house-hr-comparison-breakdown-small-businesses) **.** Time data should be kept in one secure, central system instead of scattered across spreadsheets and paper timecards, because you’ll need those records for at least three years. Also, be sure to pick a system that can add locations and employees without forcing a switch when your business grows.

A slick app is great. A real person who can fix a[payroll problem](https://www.bbsi.com/technology#timekeeping) is better.


## How Does a PEO Strengthen Attendance Tracking?


A PEO (professional employer organization) provides payroll, benefits, compliance assistance, and other HR services to small and midsize businesses.


And it’s hardly a niche arrangement: according to[NAPEO](https://napeo.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/PEOIndustryFootprint_WhitePaper2026.pdf) , “At the end of 2025, 502 PEOs served 5.4 million worksite employees (WSEs) at 233,000 client businesses.”


Software captures the data. A PEO helps you put it to work. Depending on the provider and the services you choose, that can include:


- Payroll processing that pulls directly from your time data
- Guidance on overtime, breaks, and leave rules as employment regulations change
- HR support when attendance problems turn into personnel issues
- Risk-management resources that help you identify and address potential problems

## Quick Summary


Attendance tracking creates the time records that drive payroll and support wage-and-hour compliance, and getting them wrong can be costly. This blog covers 9 features to look for in attendance tracking software, compares the time and attendance options major PEOs offer, and explains how a PEO helps businesses turn accurate time data into fewer payroll errors and less compliance risk.

## Attendance Tracking Software FAQs


##### What is attendance tracking software?


Attendance tracking software records when employees clock in, clock out, and take breaks, creating the time records employers need for payroll. Many tools also track PTO, flag overtime, and sync hours directly to payroll.


##### What features matter most in attendance tracking software?


Look for flexible, customizable clock-in options, PTO tracking, overtime and break alerts, payroll integration, and tools that help prevent time theft. Depending on your workforce, that could include geofencing or biometrics, as well as alternatives like device-specific clock-in settings, unique QR codes, or selfie capture at the time of a punch. The right solution should give you flexibility to choose the methods that best fit how and where your employees work.


##### How can a PEO help with attendance tracking?


A PEO pairs timekeeping tools with payroll processing, HR support, and compliance guidance. That combination helps businesses act on their time data and stay compliant as rules change.
